articles.title: Supreme Court rejects Romualdez bid to stop Ombudsman probe
articles.summary: In a statement on Wednesday, November 4, the high court ruled that Romualdez’s petition for certiorari has become moot following the formal filing of criminal charges against him before the…

blocks.text: November 4, 2026 | 4:43pm
The logo of the Supreme Court at the Supreme Court Building in Manila.
Philstar.com / Ian Laqui

MANILA, Philippines — The Supreme Court (SC) has dismissed the petition of detained former House Speaker Martin Romualdez challenging the preliminary investigation conducted by the Office of the Ombudsman over his plunder charge.

In a statement on Wednesday, November 4, the high court ruled that Romualdez’s petition for certiorari had become moot following the formal filing of criminal charges against him before the Sandiganbayan.

Romualdez challenged the preliminary investigation conducted by the Ombudsman, raising objections to the anti-graft body's application for a preliminary hold departure order and a freeze order against him, as well as the alleged inclusion of inadmissible evidence. Romualdez filed the petition on July 31.

The high tribunal also denied the lawmaker's prayer for a temporary restraining order and a writ of preliminary injunction, which aimed to halt the Ombudsman from proceeding with the preliminary investigation.

“The SC ruled that the petition has become moot, or no longer needs to be resolved, because a plunder charge had already been filed against Romualdez before the Sandiganbayan, where he was arraigned and pleaded not guilty,” the Supreme Court’s statement read.
“The SC also found no exceptional circumstances that would justify resolving the petition despite its having become moot,” it added.
Philstar.com has reached out to the Office of the Ombudsman for comment, but it has yet to reply.
Romualdez is currently detained at the Quezon City Jail in Payatas over a non-bailable plunder charge involving P7.44 billion linked to flood control projects.

articles.title: Supreme Court finds Martin Romualdez's bid to halt Ombudsman's probe moot
articles.summary: The Supreme Court (SC) has junked the bid of former Speaker and Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez to stop the Ombudsman"s preliminary investigation against him for being moot.

blocks.text: Published November 4, 2026 4:39pm

The Supreme Court (SC) has junked the bid of former Speaker and Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez to stop the Ombudsman’s preliminary investigation against him for being moot, or no longer needs to be resolved.

The High Tribunal made the ruling on Tuesday, November 4, with Romualdez already facing a P7.4 billion plunder charge alongside former House appropriations panel chairperson Zaldy Co of Ako Bicol party-list, his personal assistant Joselyn Tragua Sereño, and Felicito Cristobal Guevarra, president of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corporation.
The charge is in connection with alleged kickbacks from government infrastructure projects particularly those on flood control.

"The SC dismissed the petition for certiorari filed by Rep. Ferdinand Martin Romualdez challenging the preliminary investigation conducted by the respondent Office of the Ombudsman, including its application for a preliminary hold departure order and freeze order against him and the alleged use of inadmissible evidence," the SC said.
"The SC also denied Romualdez's prayer for a temporary restraining order and/or a writ of preliminary injunction to stop the respondent from continuing the preliminary investigation," it added.

"The SC ruled that the petition has become moot, or no longer needs to be resolved, because a plunder charge had already been filed against Romualdez before the Sandiganbayan, where he was arraigned and pleaded not guilty,” the High Tribunal said.
The SC said there are no “exceptional circumstances” that would justify resolving the petition despite its having become moot.
Romualdez, who is detained in New Quezon City jail in Payatas, has since filed a petition for bail to secure temporary liberty amid a plunder case leveled against him.
The hearing on Romualdez’s petition for bail is still ongoing.
GMA News Online has reached out to Romualdez’s camp for comment and will publish it as soon as it becomes available. —NB, GMA News

articles.title: Ombudsman suspends 8 DPWH personnel amid Surigao del Norte flood control probe
articles.summary: The Office of the Ombudsman has issued a suspension order on eight personnel of the Department of Public Works (DPWH) in Surigao del Norte amid the ongoing Ombudsman probe on the flood control…

blocks.text: Published November 4, 2026 4:23pm

The Office of the Ombudsman has issued a suspension order on eight personnel of the Department of Public Works (DPWH) in Surigao del Norte amid the ongoing Ombudsman probe on the flood control projects in the area.
Placed under preventive suspension without pay for six months at the maximum are:

items: Annie Dela Vega, DPWH Regional Office 11 District Engineer
Federico Gotico III, Engineer III of the DPWH Surigao del Norte 1st District Engineering Office (DEO)
Demilyn Castrence, Engineer III of the DPWH Surigao del Norte 1st DEO
Quintinano Armendariz Jr., Engineer III of the DPWH Surigao del Norte 1st DEO
Edward Tinio all Engineer III of the DPWH Surigao del Norte 1st DEO
Florencio Sulana, Engineer II
Acting Chief of Quality Assurance
Ricky Arciga, Engineer II
Jerome Sulapas, Accountant III

blocks.text: The Ombudsman said these individuals are facing administrative complaints over alleged conduct prejudicial to the best interest of the service, grave misconduct, and serious dishonesty, and that “sufficient grounds exist to impose preventive suspension on respondents.”

“Without delving into the merits of the case and based on the evidence submitted by complainant, the allegations against Respondents appear to be supported by strong evidence at this stage,” the Ombudsman said.

The Ombudsman’s Field Investigation Office 2, acting as the complainant, alleges that substantially incomplete projects were fully paid by the DPWH under the respondents’ watch, to the detriment of the government.
The Independent Commission for Infrastructure (ICI) earlier submitted as evidence the list of reportedly completed DPWH projects in the area, that turned out to be incomplete.

“The preventive suspension was imposed pending the resolution of the administrative cases, as a precautionary measure against possible abuse of the prerogatives of the respondents’ current offices in relation to the case,” the Ombudsman added.
GMA News Online has reached out to DPWH Region 11 for comment and will publish them as soon as it is available. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: M&S takes more than a year to recover from cyber-attack as profits bounce back to £355m
articles.summary:
Sales and profit from clothing and homeware remain below two years ago but ‘brand is in good health’

Marks & Spencer has said a

blocks.text: Marks & Spencer has said a devastating cyber-attack that shut down its website last year continued to hurt clothing sales over the summer, more than a year after the hack.

The retailer said profits bounced back to £355m in the six months to 26 September from only £3.4m a year before as it partly recovered from the hack. The attack, which began over Easter 2025, forced it to shut its website, which sells clothing and homewares, for more than six weeks.
Total sales over the half year across the food to fashion group rose 16.2% to £9.2bn.

However, M&S said sales and profit from its clothing and homewares arm remained below two years ago as “availability was constrained due to the longer than expected impact of manual ordering processes following the incident, while profitability was diluted by an increased mix of online sales which have higher fulfilment costs”.
The retailer has previously explained that its team of buyers had to calculate demand and make orders to suppliers without the help of their usual technology and detailed information last year.
Stuart Machin, the chief executive of M&S, said: “We are broadening our appeal and the brand is in good health, but the results fell short of their potential and show there is a lot more to do.”

The company said it had been able to take a bigger share of a declining clothing market despite the availability problems, which were now resolved, but “market conditions remain challenging”. Clothing, beauty and homewares sales rose 17.5% to almost £2bn in the half year compared with the same period last year, which was affected by the hack.
Performance is expected to improve in the second half as M&S said availability has now recovered “creating a better balance between core and seasonal stock”.

M&S’s food business increased sales by almost 14% to £5.2bn in the half year as it opened seven new stores and expanded or refurbished others. M&S said it was gaining share on everyday items such as meat, dairy and fresh produce after investing £50m in keeping prices down and improving quality.

The group’s Ocado joint venture also swung to a half-year profit of £25.6m from a loss of £3.1m a year before as sales rose 16% and it improved the efficiency of its deliveries
M&S said it expected to cut £120m in costs this year across technology, logistics and stores. It said this would partly offset new costs, including £35m related to a new packaging levy.

articles.title: Sotto seeks stricter Senate rules on prolonged absences
articles.summary: Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente "Tito" Sotto has filed a resolution seeking clearer rules on the prolonged and unauthorized absences of senators, citing complaints filed before the Committee on…

blocks.text: November 4, 2026 | 4:14pm
Sen. Tito Sotto during the impeachment proceedings against Vice President Sara Duterte on Oct. 12, 2026.
Senate PRIB
MANILA, Philippines — Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente “Tito” Sotto III has filed a resolution recommending the revision of Senate rules on prolonged and unauthorized absences.
Sotto said that “such absenteeism and neglect of duty is deemed a waste of taxpayer funds,” citing complaints filed before the Committee on Ethics.
He added that public officials "must be accountable to the people they serve and must serve with utmost responsibility, integrity, loyalty and efficiency."

Four lawmakers have been absent from Senate sessions, including fugitive Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court for alleged crimes against humanity, including murder.
Serving as chief of the Philippine National Police during former President Rodrigo Duterte’s term, Dela Rosa is accused of helping carry out killings associated with Duterte’s war on drugs.
Authorities have offered a P50 million reward for information leading to his capture and intensified their manhunt following the expiration of the week-long deadline for his arrest.
Sens. Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta, meanwhile, are detained at the New Quezon City Jail over separate plunder charges.
Estrada is alleged to have received kickbacks from anomalous flood control projects, while Marcoleta faces charges related to P75 million worth of undisclosed campaign donations.
Sen. Loren Legarda has similarly received complaints for plunder and graft but has been on medical leave since August 3.

All three absentee lawmakers are not currently receiving their salaries and Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses. Their regular staff, according to Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian, continue to receive pay.

articles.title: Democrats aim to sweep most US governor elections after wins in key states
articles.summary: Party sees historic victories with Gina Hinojosa’s win in Texas and Georgia’s Keisha Lance Bottoms becoming first Black female governor in US

blocks.text: Voters across the US have elected Democrats to lead many of the biggest states in the nation, marking a sea change in traditional Republican strongholds such as Georgia and Texas in what could have a profound effect on Donald Trump’s remaining term and the 2028 presidential election.

From Keisha Lance Bottoms’ victory in Georgia, making the former Atlanta mayor the first Black woman to be elected governor of any state, to Amy Acton’s win in reliably red Ohio, the results represented a repudiation of Trump, rank corruption in Washington and the power of billionaires to shape American politics. Democrats aimed to win a majority of governorships in the US, something they have not done since the 2006 midterm elections.

One of the biggest prizes of the night was the Texas governorship, with Democratic state representative Gina Hinojosa unseating Republican incumbent Greg Abbott in a stunning upset. Hinojosa will be the first Latina governor of the state, and the first Democrat elected to the Texas governorship in 30 years.

Like Hinojosa’s win, considered unthinkable in the aftermath of Trump’s 2024 victory in Texas, Lance Bottoms’ win in Georgia against billionaire Rick Jackson also represented a stunning flip of a Republican stronghold, where the GOP has held the governor’s office and both chambers of the state legislature for more than 20 years.

In Ohio, Democrat Acton defeated Republican Vivek Ramaswamy. The campaign drew national attention after Ramaswamy’s campaign aired a much-maligned ad featuring Acton’s estranged mother, who lost custody of her children after her husband was accused of sexually abusing Acton as a child, sharply criticizing her daughter. Acton is the first Democrat elected governor in the state since 2006, and the first woman elected governor of Ohio.

Iowa Democrat Rob Sand pulled off an upset against Republican Zach Lahn, marking a major step towards the party rebuilding its standing in a state that has voted for Donald Trump three times and where the GOP has dominated state politics in recent years.

And in Wisconsin, Democrat David Crowley defeated Republican Tom Tiffany to become the state’s first Black governor. Crowley, who withdrew from the race only to rejoin at the urging of the outgoing Democratic governor, Tony Evers, overcame a massive fundraising gap to win the governorship.
With about a third of the votes still to be counted in Arizona and Alaska, Democrats Katie Hobbs and Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins had wide leads in those states.

Democrats also racked up gubernatorial victories in Pennsylvania, where popular incumbent Josh Shapiro handily defeated Stacy Garrity, and New York, where Kathy Hochul sailed to re-election. Democrat Deb Haaland was elected governor of New Mexico, making her the first Native American woman to win a governorship, while Xavier Becerra, also a Democrat, became California’s first elected Latino governor.
In Florida, Byron Donalds, Republican congressman and a strong Trump ally, edged out the former Republican turned Democrat David Jolly, becoming the Sunshine state’s first Black governor.

While media attention has focused intensely on the battle to control the US Congress, and whether Democrats could not only flip the House of Representatives but also win most of the Senate, upsets in gubernatorial races in traditionally Republican states could reset the map before the 2028 presidential contest.
Most of the so-called swing states that help determine who wins the White House – including Michigan and Wisconsin – are among the 36 states electing governors in Tuesday’s midterm elections.

The first two years of Donald Trump’s second term as president have underscored the roles Democratic governors play in serving as a bulwark against Trump’s most excessive policies, including by filing lawsuits and other executive actions. While rules differ state by state, some governors appoint election officials who oversee elections, and can sign legislation to protect voter rights.
Republicans have held a majority of governorships since the 2010 election.

articles.title: Sandiganbayan orders BJMP officials to testify on Romualdez's detention status
articles.summary: Sandiganbayan Third Division Clerk of Court Dennis Pulma said the order was issued amid reports that the former Speaker, who is facing plunder charges in connection with alleged kickbacks from…

blocks.text: Published November 4, 2026 4:02pm

The Sandiganbayan Third Division has ordered officials of the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) to testify before the anti-graft court on Thursday regarding the status of Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez in detention.

Sandiganbayan Third Division Clerk of Court Dennis Pulma said the order was issued amid reports that the former Speaker, who is facing plunder charges in connection with alleged kickbacks from government funds, was being allowed to leave detention at the New Quezon City jail.

Romualdez is facing a P7.4 billion plunder charge alongside former House appropriations panel chairperson Zaldy Co of Ako Bicol party-list, his personal assistant Joselyn Tragua Sereño, and Felicito Cristobal Guevarra, president of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corporation.

“In light of the recent online news articles, the Sandiganbayan Third Division has issued a Resolution ordering Jail Superintendent Maria Lourdes P. Pacion and Medical Officer Henry N. Fabro, both of BJMP City Jail-Male Dormitory, Payatas, Q.C., to personally appear and testify tomorrow, November 5, 2026, at 8:30 a.m., re: the current status of accused Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez's custody at BJMP Payatas,” Pulma said in a statement.
The BJMP earlier said it is investigating the reports that Romualdez has been able to leave detention and come back as he pleases.

At the same time, the BJMP has also assured the public that Romualdez has always been in detention by releasing a video of Romualdez, in his detainee uniform, walking around the New Quezon City jail building. —NB, GMA News

articles.title: Barbers: VP Sara's defense team unlikely to overturn prosecution's evidence
articles.summary: The defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte is unlikely to overturn the bank records and her other declarations under oath that the prosecution presented as evidence against her during the trial,…

blocks.text: Published November 4, 2026 3:58pm

The defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte is unlikely to overturn the bank records and her other declarations under oath that the prosecution presented as evidence against her during the trial, House prosecution panel spokesperson Rep. Robert Ace Barbers said Wednesday.

Barbers cited the financial records of the Vice President and her husband, including Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth, bank transaction and bank deposit records, insurance payment records, income tax returns, and corporate records of their business interests, which financial forensic expert Atty. Alex Cabrera reviewed.

“These are documents, sworn declarations by no less than the Vice President, as well as records submitted to the different government agencies such as ITRs (income tax returns) and bank records. Bank records will never lie,” he said in a press conference.

“I don't think the banks will deny the existence of outstanding balances of the Vice President that they reported before the impeachment court. We're thinking how the defense will controvert the evidence presented by the prosecution, and I personally believe they don't have evidence to controvert ours," he added.

Aside from bank records, Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura also testified before the Senate impeachment court that P4.4 billion worth of covered and suspicious transactions were recorded under the bank accounts owned by the Vice President and her husband.

“Mabigat ang ebidensya at napakahirap pasinungalingan o pabulaanan itong mga ebidensyang ito. And so again, I'd like to say it's going to be difficult for the defense to dispute or probably even rebut the evidence we have presented,” Barbers added.
(Plain denials won’t work on these documents.)
The Vice President’s non-divestment in businesses where she or her husband has an interest, Barbers said, is an offense just as grave as the undeclared assets.
He cited the following business interests of the Vice President as declared in her joint SALNs with her husband since she became Vice President in 2022:

items: Metro City Chow Foods Corp., formerly City Hall King Chow Foods Corp. as stated in her 2023, 2024, and 2025 SALNs
Gencorp Industries Inc. formerly Timesquare Bee Foods Corp. and Great Jolly Times Food, as stated in her 2024 and 2025 SALNs
Davao New Royal Taipan Corp. (formerly Davao Emerging Taipans Corporation), as stated in her 2022 and 2023 SALNs
Timesquare Bee Foods Corp. (formerly Great Joly Times Foods Corp.), as stated in her 2022 and 2023 SALNs
Tapang At Malasakit Alliançe for the Philippines, Inc., as stated in her 2022 and 2023 SALNs

blocks.text: “Kapag mismo ang may akda [ng iyong] SALN., hindi mo maaaring balewalain lamang. Kapag Bise Presidente ka, hindi pwedeng 'yung isang kamay mo ay namamahala sa gobyerno, habang 'yung kabilang kamay ay namamahala naman sa negosyo,” Barbers said.
(If it is your SALN declaration, it is something that we cannot ignore. As the Vice President, you cannot be a public official on one hand and a businesswoman on the other.)

Barbers said that GenCorp. Industries Inc. winning P35 million in government contracts with the Davao City local government headed by the Vice President’s brother, Mayor Sebastian Duterte, is a textbook case of conflict of interest.

“Based on the opinion of Atty. Cabrera, if the Vice President was listed as one of the shareholders of GenCorp, it would not win government contracts. Let us remember that GenCorp.’s sales in 2021 were P28 million and it climbed to P300 million in 2022, the year that she became Vice President. By 2025, GenCorp’s sales already reached P520 million, and it bought P150 million worth of equipment when it only had P1.25 million capital,” he said.
“Who owns GenCorp and where is its huge sales coming from? If that is not a conflict of interest, I don’t know what it is,” he added.
The impeachment trial of the Vice President resumes on November 9.
GMA News Online reached out to the camp of Duterte for comment and will publish it once available.

The camp of Vice President Duterte earlier objected to the prosecution’s offer of evidence by arguing that these are inadmissible because the documents were neither cited in the Articles of Impeachment nor attached to the original complaints, and/or that these lacked evidentiary support or testimony from a competent witness.—AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Democrats win control of Senate as US voters reject Trump’s agenda
articles.summary: Republicans routed as Democrats gain powerful new leverage over Trump for remainder of his presidency

blocks.text: Democrats have regained control of the US Senate, routing Republicans nationwide with historic victories that will give them powerful new leverage over Donald Trump for the remainder of his presidency.
Together with their likely triumph in the House of Representatives, Democrats are expected to have full control of Congress beginning next year, for the first time since 2022.
“Wow! Wow! Now, against all odds, we Democrats have won the Senate,” the minority leader Chuck Schumer said in Washington DC. “We have five words for the American people: relief is on the way.”

The Democrats will return to power after their candidates won in a host of states where they hadn’t had success in years, if not decades, including Maine, South Carolina, North Carolina, Ohio, Texas, Iowa and Kansas, according to the Associated Press.

Democrats will soon have the ability to hold up not just Trump’s legislative agenda, but also any appointments he makes to his cabinet or the federal judiciary – including the supreme court, where conservatives have a 6-3 majority.

Thus far, Democrats have won 54 seats, and Republicans 42. Vote counting is ongoing in Alaska, where Democrat Mary Peltolia is vying to beat two-term Republican Dan Sullivan. It may takes days to determine the outcome of that race.

Republicans have thus far failed to unseat any of the Democrats they viewed as vulnerable after the 2024 election, including in Michigan, New Hampshire, Georgia and Minnesota. However, Republicans have been re-elected or have held on to seats in dozens of red states, many of which are in the south or midwest.

But even those victories served as warning signals for the party. The Republican incumbent Ashley Moody won in Florida, but only by about three percentage points. Other Republicans have won recent elections by double digits in the former presidential battleground, which has become deeply conservative in recent years.

Julia Letlow has triumphed in the race for the open Senate seat in Louisiana, another Republican stronghold, but the margin of her Democratic opponent is just two percentage points. Trump won the state by about 22 percentage points two years ago.
The election is a stunning reversal from 2024, when voters sent Trump back to the White House and gave his allies a 53-seat majority in the Senate, ending four years of Democratic control.

In the wake of that election, it seemed unlikely that Democrats would be back in charge any time soon – most states scheduled to hold Senate elections in 2026 were strongholds of one party or another, and the tendency of voters to split their tickets between parties in congressional elections has declined in recent years.

Democrats initially named as their Senate targets Republican-held seats in North Carolina, Ohio, Alaska and Maine. The GOP, meanwhile, hoped to claim Democratic-held seats in Georgia and Michigan – both of which voted for Trump – as well as New Hampshire and Minnesota, which Kamala Harris carried by relatively weak margins.

But Trump made a series of deeply unpopular policy decisions, and his approval ratings slumped over time, particularly on handling of the economy and immigration, which were previously two of his best issues.

His decision to attack Iran and send federal agents to conduct highly public immigration raids, which resulted in the killings of two US citizens in Minneapolis, further alienated voters. As gas prices rose due to the conflict in the Middle East, Democrats became confident about winning Senate elections in Texas, Kansas and Iowa.

“Republicans had a choice of following Trump over the cliff, even though Trump policies made American families’ pain much worse,” Schumer said. “We never wavered. We listened to the American people, what they wanted. We talked to them. We sat down in their kitchens, in their living rooms, and said, ‘What should we do?’ And they told us, and we listened.”

The result is a wave of victories unheard of in modern American politics. Kansas has not sent a Democrat to the Senate since 1932, and Texas since 1988. In South Carolina, 38 years have passed since a Democrat won a Senate race, while in Iowa and North Carolina, it’s been 18 years.

Trump’s meddling in the Republican primaries also seemed to backfire. He condemned North Carolina’s Republican senator Thom Tillis for opposing his main domestic policy legislation, leading him to announce his retirement. The Democratic nominee, former governor Roy Cooper, easily won the race to replace him.

Trump also endorsed scandal-plagued Texas attorney general Ken Paxton over the state’s longtime US senator John Cornyn, causing the incumbent to lose his primary, and giving Democrats what they believed to be a rare opening in one of the country’s most influential Republican strongholds. Democratic state representative James Talarico won that seat by a double-digit margin, according to the AP.

After the sudden death of South Carolina’s longtime Republican senator Lindsey Graham, Trump backed the bid of his sister, Darline Graham, to serve a full term, even though she’d never won elected office and there were other Republicans in the race. Graham has lost to Democrat Annie Andrews by a margin of about four percentage points.

Republicans now have less than two months remaining with unified control of government, and there’s been speculation they could quickly try to confirm a new conservative appointment to the supreme court, if one of the sitting justices retired.

Asked to weigh in on that possibility, Schumer said: “I hope Republicans learn the lesson that they failed to see up to tonight. Listen to the American people … They want us to focus on, again, costs, chaos, corruption.”

articles.title: Democrats’ blue wave and a bad night for Trump: key US midterms takeaways
articles.summary:
Republicans suffered historic losses, Democrats won control of Congress – and Trump backed away from losing candidates

Democrats swept

blocks.text: Democrats swept key US midterm races on Tuesday evening, flipping long-held Republican seats and securing a majority in Congress after voters rebuked Donald Trump’s policies at the ballot box.
In an unexpected performance, Democrats defeated incumbent Republicans candidates for historically conservative Senate seats in Iowa, Kansas, North Carolina, South Carolina and Texas.

Polls indicated Democrats were leading in competitive races but failed to fully predict the extent of the party’s massive wins. Voters have expressed disapproval of Trump’s performance as president, especially related to the cost of living.

Despite telling voters to act as though he was still on the ballot, Trump dismissed concerns the results are a response to his presidency, saying he would have “won in a landslide” had he been on the ballot.
Here are the key takeaways from the results:

items: 1. The blue wave Democrats saw their hoped-for “blue wave” become reality by flipping seven Senate seats, more than two dozen House seats and expanding the number of Democratic governors.Shortly after polls closed, Democrats saw winning streaks in closely watched Senate races. Before midnight, the Associated Press had declared Democrats would hold the majority in Congress’s upper chamber. Less than two hours later, they secured the House.With control over both chambers, Democrats gain the authority to push back on Trump’s agenda.Tuesday’s evening results were sweeping, with states and districts that voted for Trump two years ago abandoning the president’s allies in the midterms. Even Republican incumbents running in comfortably red areas, such as Florida, were locked in close races with Democrats.

2. Republicans suffer historic losses Democrats’ win was underscored by Republicans’ historic losses across the country.For the first time in 94 years, Kansas saw a Democrat win a Senate seat, with Adam Hamilton defeating Roger Marshall.Republicans lost a South Carolina Senate seat for the first time in nearly 30 years when Dr. Annie Andrews defeated Darline Graham – the sister of the late senator Lindsey Graham and a close ally of Trump.James Talarico, a progressive Democratic newcomer, defeated Ken Paxton, the state’s conservative attorney general, in Texas’s Senate race, ending Republicans’ 38-year streak.Iowa and North Carolina also hadn’t elected a Democratic senator since 2008.

3. Trump walks back claims to be on the ballotAfter suffering major losses, Trump asserted he “wasn’t on the Ballot” but “would have won IN A LANDSLIDE” if he was – a reversal from his request that voters act as though he was.For weeks, Trump had encouraged supporters to vote as though he was a candidate on the ballot, in the hopes of generating support for Republicans. But on Tuesday night, he dismissed concerns that the midterm results were a reflection of that.“I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE! Thank you for your attention to this matter,” Trump said.He reiterated his claim to the New York Times, saying: “I wasn’t on the ticket, and because I wasn’t on the ticket, we couldn’t get enough people out to vote.The US president, who has a long history of making false election fraud claims, also told the newspaper he was “absolutely willing” to accept the results of the midterms.

4. Democrats outperform pollsIn the lead-up to the election, polls indicated Democrats were poised to win the House and possibly the Senate, with Democratic candidates holding narrow leads over Republicans in competitive Senate races.But pre-election polls were more reserved about Democrats’ win, in part due to the failed predictions over the 2024 presidential election.In the Kansas Senate race, pre-election polls indicated Democrat Adam Hamilton had a small lead over Republican Roger Marshall. But pollsters from the Washington Post warned that the prediction could be misleading because Democratic voters were more likely to respond than Republicans.

5. Trump’s handpicked candidates lose In another example of voters’ rebuke of Trump, the US president’s handpicked candidates in key races lost their bids to Democrats.Historically, candidates endorsed by Trump perform well in primaries and general elections. But this time around, those candidates could not convince voters to cast their ballot for them.In the Texas Senate race, Ken Paxton lost – even after securing Trump’s support in a contentious primary.In the South Carolina Senate race, Darline Graham failed to defeat Dr. Annie Andrews, even after Trump elevated Graham to take over her late brother’s seat and campaigned for her heavily.Trump chose Michael Whatley to fend off Democrat Roy Cooper in North Carolina’s Senate race, yet Cooper defeated Whatley.

articles.title: Immigration intercepts 2 Filipinos bound for conflict zones
articles.summary: The Bureau of Immigration has intercepted two Filipino men attempting to leave the country after uncovering suspicious online recruitment schemes that promised thousands of dollars in salaries and…

blocks.text: November 4, 2026 | 3:45pm
One of the two Pinoys intercepted by the Bureau of Immigration after attempting to leave the country for alleged jobs in conflict zones.
Bureau of Immigration / Released

MANILA, Philippines — The Bureau of Immigration has intercepted two Filipino men attempting to leave the country after uncovering suspicious online recruitment schemes that promised thousands of dollars in salaries and signing bonuses for jobs in armed conflict zones.
In a statement on Wednesday, November 4, the bureau said the separate interceptions occurred on October 24 and October 27.
The first passenger, an unemployed former protection agent and security guard, was intercepted on October 24.

During questioning, he revealed that he had been recruited through Facebook and subsequently contacted via WhatsApp. The recruiter allegedly promised him a $12,000 (P762,174) signing bonus upon arrival, alongside a monthly salary of $2,500 (P158,778.75), with all travel expenses covered.
Three days later, on October 27, immigration officers stopped a second Filipino man who initially claimed he was traveling to Hong Kong for a vacation sponsored by a friend.

Further inquiry showed that he had also responded to a Facebook job advertisement before communicating with the recruiter via WhatsApp, where he was offered an overseas position promising a $27,000 (P1,714,810.50) upfront payment and a $3,000 (P190,534.50) monthly salary without requiring any initial out-of-pocket expenses.

The bureau noted that both cases followed a pattern of unverified recruiters using lucrative financial promises to entice victims into travel arrangements to destinations affected by active armed conflicts.
On October 17, the bureau also stopped three Filipinos in Davao who attempted to leave the country for alleged military and border guard work in Eastern Europe.

articles.title: Win Gatchalian pushes for law banning public officials kin from getting gov't contracts
articles.summary: Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian on Wednesday stressed the need to pass into law the measure seeking to prohibit relatives of public officials from entering into government contracts.

blocks.text: Published November 4, 2026 3:40pm
Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian on Wednesday stressed the need to pass into law the measure seeking to prohibit relatives of public officials from entering into government contracts.

“Importante na maisabatas natin ito sa lalong madaling panahon para masiguro natin na ang pondo ng bayan ay napupunta sa mga programa at proyekto na makakatulong sa taong-bayan at hindi lang sa mga kamag-anak ng mga nasa kapangyarihan,” Gatchalian said in a statement.

(It’s important that we enact this into law as soon as possible to ensure that public funds go to programs and projects that will benefit the people, rather than just the relatives of those in power.)
In September, the Senate approved on third and final reading Senate Bill No. 1962, or the Government Contracting and Procurement Integrity Act.

Under the measure, relatives of any covered public official or personnel within the fourth civil degree of consanguinity or affinity would be barred from participating in or entering into any government contract, as well as from engaging in subcontracting, consortiums, joint ventures or similar business arrangements for the performance of a government contract.

This would apply to contracts between private entities and government agencies or instrumentalities involving supplies, materials, machinery, equipment and services, as well as infrastructure, joint venture and public-private partnership projects and other similar agreements. —NB, GMA News

articles.title: Progressive Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate race to become first Muslim US senator
articles.summary:
Democrat defeats Mike Rogers in race marked by Islamophobic attacks from Trump and Republican allies

Abdul El-Sayed, the doctor and progressive insurgent, has made history in winning the…

blocks.text: Abdul El-Sayed, the doctor and progressive insurgent, has made history in winning the closely watched US Senate race in Michigan, defeating the Republican Mike Rogers and becoming the country’s first Muslim senator.
El-Sayed’s victory adds to a decisive Democratic majority in the Senate after the party wrested control of the upper chamber on Tuesday.
El-Sayed declared victory in Michigan’s US Senate race early on Wednesday at the Michigan Democrats’ headquarters in Detroit.
“You welcomed me in your homes, your churches, your synagogues,” El-Sayed said.
He credited a movement built over a year and a half of campaigning in Michigan’s biggest cities and smallest towns, and said voters gave him strength in his lowest moments.

His opponent and detractors, including Donald Trump, led a largely Islamophobic campaign against him, often pointing to his name and faith, including the president alleging he was a “jihadist” and that he would need to walk through a metal detector to get into the Senate.
El-Sayed said his denigrators chose to be divisive rather than address the cost of gas and groceries because they didn’t have an answer to the problems he said they created.
“They want an America that is too small for some of us,” El-Sayed said. “We know that America is big enough for all of us.”
Rogers, a former congressman who was endorsed by Donald Trump and ran as his close ally, previously lost the 2024 Senate race to Elissa Slotkin by roughly 0.3 percentage points.

This time he ran against El-Sayed, a former Wayne county health director who upset the Democratic establishment favorite Haley Stevens in the primary earlier this year. He advocated for the Medicare for All proposal for universal healthcare and called for an end to US military aid for Israel.
Both candidates were running to succeed Gary Peters, an outgoing Democratic senator who has held the seat since 2015.

Republicans cast the general election as a referendum on the Democratic left, and El-Sayed’s nomination prompted Trump to call him a “communist”, and to slander him as a “jihadist” and member of the Egyptian Muslim Brotherhood.
The race was seen as a test of whether a progressive insurgent could win a swing state.

The pro-Israel lobby Aipac, through its Super Pac United Democracy Project, spent roughly $30m in the primary trying to stop El-Sayed, a record for a single race. More than $220m in total ad spending had been poured into the general election by mid-October by both parties, according to AdImpact.
In his victory speech, he said: “We want our taxes spent here, for schools here, and healthcare here, and infrastructure here. We don’t want our money sent to do apartheid, or genocide, or war.”

Rogers had backed Trump’s aggressive tariff policy and war with Iran, before breaking with the president on both in the closing weeks of the campaign, calling for an end to the US-Canada trade war and for swift conclusion to the Iran conflict. He has previously opposed the Affordable Care Act, defended the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement, and has repeated Trump’s false claims about the 2020 election.

Republicans had sought to portray El-Sayed as too far left for a swing state. A Fox News poll in August found 54% of Michigan voters thought his positions were too extreme, though 51% also said Rogers was too close to Trump.

articles.title: PH tries to ease tensions with China as ASEAN Summit nears
articles.summary: Chinese Premier Li Qiang is expected to participate in the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits. President Marcos had said he wants President Xi Jinping to visit the Philippines, if the South China…

items: The Philippines and China engaged in diplomatic talks to ease tensions ahead of the 49th ASEAN Summit, with both foreign ministers emphasizing the importance of dialogue and peaceful dispute resolution.
Despite efforts for a reset in relations, confrontations in the West Philippine Sea and inflammatory remarks from Chinese officials have continued to strain bilateral ties.
The Philippines remains committed to a stable relationship with China while pursuing an independent foreign policy, as highlighted by Foreign Secretary Lazaro's statements ahead of the ASEAN Summit.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines — With over a week to go before world leaders converge in Manila for the 49th Association of Southeast Asian (ASEAN) Summit, the Philippines and China sought to ease bilateral tensions — at least diplomatically — through a call between its foreign ministers.

In a statement on Wednesday, November 4, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) said Foreign Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro and Chinese Foreign Ministers Wang Yi had a “frank, pragmatic, and constructive” phone call to discuss “the state of bilateral ties at length.”

“The two ministers shared the understanding that such a relationship rests on three principles: first, that both sides maintain diplomacy and dialogue; second, that both sides avoid actions and rhetoric that could needlessly undermine relations or heighten tensions; and third, that both sides resolve disputes peacefully and manage differences responsibly,” said the DFA.

While Beijing has yet to release an official readout on the call, state news agency Xinhua said that during the meeting, Wang “urged the Philippine side to faithfully implement its one-China policy and exercise prudence in its words and actions on maritime issues.”

Lazaro and Wang last spoke formally in July 2026, on the sidelines of the ASEAN Foreign Ministers meeting. That meeting was preceded by a confrontation in Ayungin (Second Thomas) Shoal that injured a Filipino soldier.

This time, the phone call is backdropped by what’s arguably the tensest time in bilateral relations yet. Chinese Ambassador to Manila Jing Quan started a maelstrom after he said the Philippines should be “fortunate” that China does not use force in its disputes with the Philippines. Lazaro summoned Jing after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said the remarks were a “threat.”

But the maelstrom raged on after that meeting. Philippine officials and the Chinese embassy in Manila, which Jing heads, continued exchanging tirades on social media and in media interviews. At the ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM) Plus, China sent only its Manila-based defense attache, who was then not received personally by China-sanctioned Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr.

Beijing accused Teodoro of supposedly getting in the way of their participation in the highest defense diplomacy engagement within ASEAN. Teodoro himself had told the media on October 23 that the invitation to China — issued by Defense Undersecretary Ignacio Madriaga — had just been sent out. The meetings, hosted in Cebu, started on October 28.
Manila will be hosting the 49th ASEAN Summit — the biggest of all events under its chairmanship — from November 16 to 18.
Marcos had signaled early on in 2026 — as Manila took on ASEAN chairmanship — that he wanted a “reset” in ties with China.

“The Philippines remains committed to a stable, predictable, mutually respectful, and mutually beneficial relationship with China, in accordance with the national interest and in pursuit of an independent foreign policy as enshrined in the Philippine Constitution,” the DFA said on Wednesday.

Marcos’ desire for a reset past the midway point of his presidency made sense especially with the ASEAN chairmanship. The bloc’s goal, set by its foreign ministers in 2023, was to finish South China Sea code of conduct (COC) talks by 2026.

The Philippines, under Marcos, started pushing back stronger against China’s encroachments in the South China Sea. It also expanded its defense network and deepened existing ties with traditional partners — moves that, at times, ruffled China’s feathers. Delimitation talks with Japan in waters north of the Philippines are believed to have, among other things, spurred Beijing’s new claims over Batanes and the waters of the Philippine province.

The Philippines remains committed to a stable, predictable, mutually respectful, and mutually beneficial relationship with China, in accordance with the national interest and in pursuit of an independent foreign policy as enshrined in the Philippine Constitution

The upcoming ASEAN Summit was highlighted in the DFA press statement, with Lazaro saying Marcos “looks forward to the participation of Chinese Premier Li Qiang in the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits in Manila.”

The President had hoped for President Xi Jinping to visit Manila, if the Code of Conduct in the South China Sea had concluded. Xi typically does not participate in the ASEAN Summit and Related Summits.

The DFA said that according to Wang, China is “anticipating” Marcos’ participation in the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen. “Both ministers assured each other that their respective leaders would be accorded the proper courtesies and assistance during these meetings,” said the DFA.
The COC is not expected to conclude by the ASEAN Summit in Manila.

According to the Xinhua report, Wang claimed that “China-Philippines relations are facing malicious interference at present” and that “a few Philippine politicians, out of political prejudice and self-interest, have repeatedly attacked and smeared China,” a barely-veiled allusion to Teodoro.

“Such deeds are irrational and intolerable, and damaging to the Philippines’ own international image, Wang said, adding that Manila should exercise greater restraint over the individuals concerned and ensure that its policy toward China reflects a rational and unified voice,” said Xinhua in its report.
The DFA press release, titled “DFA Statement on Stable and Predictable Philippines-China Relations,” focused on assurances that Manila wants to calm ties with Beijing.

“The discussion also covered other matters of concern, including maritime issues, but focused on returning the relationship to an even keel and on upholding the 1975 Joint Communiqué, which remains the enduring basis of Philippines-China cooperation and of the Philippines’ One China Policy,” said the DFA.

Yet as attempts at a reset commenced, confrontations in the West Philippine Sea, an area that includes the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone, continued to happen. China’s political pressure also stepped up, with the sanction of Teodoro and his family over his statements against Beijing. The Chinese embassy in Manila continued with strong, sometimes inflammatory statements on its social media accounts against Philippine officials, including nationally-elected legislators. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Four tankers destroyed by naval mines in Strait of Hormuz, Iran's IRGC says
articles.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says the vessels had hit sea mines while trying to cross a prohibited route.

blocks.text: Four oil tankers were destroyed after hitting naval sea mines, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Wednesday, a day after US officials said the US military had launched strikes on the country.

The IRGC said two of the vessels were still burning, and two additional tankers had been seized, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency. It said they were trying to travel through a prohibited southern route in the Strait of Hormuz.

The BBC has not independently verified the IRGC's claim, which came as US voters punished Republicans at the midterm elections, leading Iran's top negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, to say the results showed Americans had said no to war.
He warned Washington not to betray its public.
The IRCG also reported three tankers had been destroyed after hitting mines early on Tuesday, and that they had shot down an MQ-9 drone over the Strait.
The earlier US strikes on Qeshm were in response to the IRGC firing on a US aircraft.

Ghalibaf, who is also Iran's parliamentary speaker, posted on X, external that the midterm results showed that whether it was "conscience or the cost of living, Americans said no to war, and we endorse this message".
"If the US govt betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our 'no' comes with a nightmare."

US President Donald Trump on Tuesday acknowledged the poor results for Republican congress members was partly due to the war on Iran and the consequent increased gas prices, but that he didn't regret launching it. He told the BBC's partner CBS News that the conflict would end "when I say it ends".

In an interview with the Financial Times ahead of the midterm elections on Tuesday, Trump suggested he was happy with the state of the conflict, and that he didn't consider them to be "really in a war".

Asked about comments by Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu that there would be another attack on Iran this week, Trump said they were "locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no need for it".
On Tuesday night, Trump told Fox News there were some people who would "love" to do a "heavy hit" on Iran.
"The only thing I can tell you with certainty, they will never have a nuclear weapon," Trump said.
Talks to end the conflict, which was triggered by joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February, have been stalled for months, with little sign of a breakthrough.
Ghalibaf told a parliamentary session on Tuesday that Iran "will not surrender" and the responsibility to prevent a war lay with the US.

"If Washington makes another strategic mistake, it should know that this time it will face a new battlefield and will be even more desperate than it is today as it searches for a way out," Ghalibaf said.
Meanwhile Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian maintained his government had been trying to resolve the crisis "through dialogue".
"No-one will benefit from this war" if fighting is restarted, he said on Tuesday.

Iran, which closed the Strait of Hormuz in response to the attack, has said it will only reopen it if the US agrees to demands contained in its peace plan. Foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei this week said the seven-step plan had been condensed, and could be implemented in two days if the US agreed.

articles.title: First 10 Australian songs inducted into the National Songbook after ‘very robust’ judging
articles.summary: Yothu Yindi’s Treaty, Midnight Oil’s Beds Are Burning and Helen Reddy’s I Am Woman are among the first songs to be honoured on new list that will grow every…

blocks.text: Midnight Oil’s Beds Are Burning, Yothu Yindi’s Treaty and Helen Reddy’s I Am Woman are among the first 10 Australian songs to be inducted into the National Songbook – a new digital archive that celebrates and preserves songs that have shaped Australia’s national cultural identity.

Launched on Wednesday night at the National Film and Sound Archive (NFSA) in Canberra, the songbook is a joint initiative between NFSA and the music rights organisation Apra Amcos. The first 10 songs were selected by a panel of 11 music experts including broadcasters Richard Kingsmill and Zan Rowe, composer Cornel Wilczek and musician Mo’Ju.
The Apra chair, Jenny Morris, and the NFSA chair, Annette Shun Wah, facilitated a “very robust conversation”, said Meagan Loader, the chief curator of the NFSA.

“There’s no such thing as a definitive list when it comes to music – you can never capture everyone’s taste – but I hope people see at least one song on there and see themselves reflected in the list,” said Loader, who was not part of the panel. “You hear some of these songs and you feel distinctly that they say something about who we are as a nation.”

The oldest song on the list is Andrew “Banjo” Paterson’s Waltzing Matilda, written by the bush poet in 1895 and later composed by Christina Macpherson. The 1927 recording “remains one of Australia’s most enduring hauntings”, the panel said.

Yothu Yindi’s Treaty – written by Dr M Yunupingu, Stuart Kellaway, Witiyana Marika, M Mununggurr, Cal Williams, G Yunupingu, Peter Garrett and Paul Kelly – was included for being a “landmark protest anthem”. Written in 1990 around a campfire, the rallying song has soundtracked generations of gatherings, from protests to dancefloors.
“I’m proud to be part of the song,” Paul Kelly told Guardian Australia. “Like the song, the process of treaty-making around the country is the work of many hands and still ongoing.”
Kelly said the song came to be when he and M Yunupingu were sitting around a campfire at Birany Birany, East Arnhem Land.

“From there it travelled through many hands – to a Darwin rehearsal room with the rest of the band, then to recording studios in Melbourne and Sydney, a hotel room in Glebe, the Midnight Oil offices with Peter Garrett, and back to Melbourne again,” he said.

Melbourne electronic producers Filthy Lucre had a “huge influence” on the track, Kelly said. “[They] took a minor hit and thoroughly re-tooled it, stripping out many of its elements, including most of the English vocals, and turning it into an international dancefloor banger that really put Yothu Yindi on the map.”

The most recent Australian song on the list is another call to arms disguised as an electronic banger: 2008’s My People by the Presets. Written by Julian Hamilton and Kim Moyes, the track is a protest song about Australia’s treatment of asylum seekers. Its lyrics – “I’m here with all of my people / locked up with all of my people” – were written as a declaration of solidarity. “Its political message may be less immediately apparent to listeners today, but its ferocity remains,” the panel said.

The Easybeats’ 1966 garage-rock anthem Friday on My Mind – written by founding members Harry Vanda and George Young – was honoured for capturing the “restless energy of a generation hungry for romance and escape”.

Ruby Hunter’s 1990 song Down City Streets, initially recorded for Archie Roach’s album Charcoal Lane, about displacement as a member of the Stolen Generations, and Helen Reddy’s feminist anthem I Am Woman were also included. Both songs were praised by the panel for their personal storytelling and for resonating with listeners after their lifetimes.
Neil Murray’s My Island Home, released by the Warumpi Band in 1987 and covered by Christine Anu in 1995, was chosen for its evolution over time and “enduring pull of home and belonging”.

Loader was personally stoked to see Midnight Oil’s Beds Are Burning – written by Peter Garrett, Rob Hirst and Jim Moginie – on the list. “I remember being a child and hearing it for the first time and understanding Australian history and culture in a whole new way,” she said. “It was almost an awakening.
“For those messages to still be so powerful and important [years later], to me that speaks volumes to the power of incredible songwriting.”

The first 10 songs are not all commercial releases. The score to 1998 film The Boys, written by avant garde jazz trio the Necks, was included for its “unsettling” and “off-kilter” qualities. And Peter Sculthorpe’s 11-minute Earth Cry, featuring William Barton playing the yidaki (didgeridoo), made the list for its ability to capture “the vastness of Australia”.
The list will continue to grow and evolve each year, with a new panel appointed to select 10 more songs.
To be eligible, the songs must have been written or co-written by an Australian Apra member, be at least a decade old, and have a demonstrable cultural impact.

“We see this first list as a great conversation starter,” Loader said. “There were a couple of commercially successful, huge songs that were a shoo-in for this list, but we decided we would let the songbook grow over time and become a conversation about what is a really significant Australian song … It’ll be really interesting to see in 10 years’ time what that songbook will look like.”
The first 10 songs inducted into the National Songbook

items: Beds Are Burning by Midnight Oil (1987)
Down City Streets by Ruby Hunter (1990)
Earth Cry by Peter Sculthorpe (1990)
Friday on My Mind by the Easybeats (1966), written by Harry Vanda and George Young
I Am Woman by Helen Reddy, written by Reddy and Ray Burton (1971)
My Island Home, written by Neil Murray and released by Warumpi Band (1987) and Christine Anu (1995)
My People by the Presets (2007)
The Boys soundtrack by The Necks (1998)
Treaty by Yothu Yindi (1991)
Waltzing Matilda (1927)

articles.title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force
articles.summary: On Wednesday morning, Delhi's air quality index reading stood at 377, in the "very poor" category.

blocks.text: Delhi is once again battling worsening air pollution as the onset of winter brings a familiar deterioration in air quality.

The city's Air Quality Index (AQI) - which measures PM2.5, fine particulate matter that can clog lungs - has crossed 300, entering the "very poor" category and raising health concerns for millions of residents.
Breathing such polluted air over prolonged periods can cause respiratory problems and worsen existing illnesses, with children and older people particularly vulnerable.
Authorities have responded by invoking Stage II of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), introducing measures to curb dust, vehicle emissions and other sources of pollution.
Delhi and neighbouring parts of northern India grapple with hazardous air every winter, particularly around Diwali, one of India's biggest festivals, which is just days away.
The festival is celebrated with lights, lamps and fireworks, which often worsen the city's already poor air quality by releasing fine particles and harmful gases into the atmosphere.

The annual pollution crisis is driven by a combination of factors, including vehicle exhaust, industrial emissions, falling temperatures, low wind speeds and the burning of crop stubble in neighbouring states.
The sharp rise in pollution follows an unusually clean October, when Delhi recorded its lowest average AQI for the month in eight years.
Experts have attributed the sudden deterioration to falling temperatures, slow winds and an increase in crop-residue burning in the neighbouring states of Punjab and Haryana.
A recent storm had brought rain and stronger winds, helping clear the air. But as the weather settled, north-westerly winds returned, carrying smoke from burning fields towards the capital.
India's pollution watchdog classifies AQI readings between 301 and 400 as "very poor", while anything above 400 is considered "severe". On Wednesday morning, Delhi's AQI stood at 377.
The index takes into account eight major pollutants, including PM2.5 - tiny particles about 30 times smaller than the width of a human hair that can penetrate deep into the lungs.
With Diwali just days away, there are concerns that fireworks could push pollution levels even higher.
Last year, Delhi woke up to a toxic haze the morning after the festival, despite a court directive to use less-polluting firecrackers.
Authorities have imposed restrictions on firecrackers over the years, including outright bans on their manufacture, sale and use, but enforcing them has proved difficult.
On Monday, India's Supreme Court allowed the manufacture, sale and use of certified green firecrackers in Delhi and neighbouring areas for a limited period.
It said the crackers could be set off only between 06:00 and 07:00 local time (00:30-01:30 GMT) and between 20:00 and 22:00 (14:30-16:30 GMT) on 7 and 8 November, during the Diwali weekend.
The court also banned fireworks within 300m of hospitals, care homes, schools and other designated silence zones.

Green firecrackers use modified chemical formulations designed to produce fewer emissions than conventional fireworks. They must carry QR codes that allow buyers and authorities to verify details of their manufacturer and certification.
But ensuring that only approved firecrackers are sold remains a major challenge.
In its latest order, the Supreme Court acknowledged that conventional firecrackers had continued to be sold as green alternatives, even when a complete ban was in place.
It has directed police to patrol designated sales areas, carry out random QR-code checks and seize illegal firecrackers.
During particularly severe pollution episodes, Delhi authorities have also introduced measures such as hybrid schooling, work-from-home arrangements and restrictions on certain vehicles.

The problem is not confined to the capital. Mumbai, India's financial hub, has also recorded elevated pollution levels over the past month, despite benefiting from coastal winds that typically help disperse pollutants.

On 24 October, Mumbai's AQI had reached 322, placing it in the "very poor" category. The spike was attributed to a combination of low wind speeds, construction dust, garbage burning, firecracker emissions and pollutants carried from neighbouring regions.
The city's air quality has improved in recent days - and it recorded an AQI of 89, classified as "satisfactory", on Wednesday. Neighbouring Navi Mumbai recorded a "moderate" AQI of 118.
The improvement follows nearly two weeks of smoggy conditions, with residents sharing photos and videos of the haze on social media.

articles.title: DFA: PH, China stress need for dialogue, mutual respect
articles.summary: The Philippines and China have emphasized the need to maintain diplomatic dialogue and mutual respect despite their differences, Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro said…
articles.byline: JEAN MANGALUZ, JP SORIANO, GMA NEWS, GMA News

blocks.text: Published November 4, 2026 2:41pm

The Philippines and China have emphasized the need to maintain diplomatic dialogue and mutual respect despite their differences, Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro said on Wednesday.

Lazaro spoke with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi following a series of heated verbal exchanges between officials of Manila and Beijing. The exchanges stemmed from Chinese Ambassador to the Philippines Jing Quan’s apparent veiled threat against the country.
“I had a telephone call with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi this afternoon and had a frank and constructive discussion on the direction of Philippines-China relations," Lazaro said in a post on X.
Both sides emphasized the need for continued diplomatic dialogue and the proper management of differences anchored on mutual respect,” she added.
In a separate statement, the DFA provided further details of the conversation, saying the two officials discussed the state of bilateral relations at length.
The call was frank, pragmatic and constructive, the DFA said.
Both officials recognized the importance of sustaining diplomatic engagement, avoiding actions and rhetoric that could heighten tensions, and resolving disputes peacefully.
The DFA said relations between the two countries should be sustained through high-level exchanges, ministry-to-ministry channels, and appropriate bilateral and regional mechanisms.
Lazaro also conveyed to Wang that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. looked forward to the participation of Chinese Premier Li Qiang in the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits in Manila.
Wang, meanwhile, said China anticipated Marcos' participation in the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China.

“The discussion also covered other matters of concern, including maritime issues, but focused on returning the relationship to an even keel and on upholding the 1975 Joint Communiqué, which remains the enduring basis of Philippines-China cooperation and of the Philippines’ One China Policy,” the DFA said.

Tensions between Manila and Beijing flared anew after Quan said China would easily win in a fight over the West Philippine Sea. Several Philippine officials subsequently urged Marcos to declare the Chinese envoy persona non grata over his remarks.
The latest diplomatic tensions came amid longstanding territorial and maritime disputes between the two countries over the West Philippine Sea, which China continues to claim largely as its own.
The tensions have prompted several Philippine business groups to call on both countries to exercise restraint.

In a joint statement, business organizations, including the Philippine Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PCCI), Employers Confederation of the Philippines (ECOP), and Federation of Filipino-Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FFCCII), urged Philippine and Chinese officials to renew diplomatic dialogue.
The DFA welcomed the business groups' appeal, describing it as a constructive contribution to efforts to manage bilateral differences.

“The DFA has consistently maintained that diplomacy, dialogue, and mutually beneficial practical cooperation can be pursued without compromising the assertion and protection of the country’s sovereignty, sovereign rights, and jurisdiction," the DFA said.
This approach provides the foundation for a stable and predictable relationship with China,” it added. — MCG, GMA News

articles.title: US midterm election results: Democrats flip House and Senate. Here's what else the data tells us
articles.summary: Democrats have won the majority in both House and Senate. Vote counts are still ongoing. DW takes a look at who voted Republican, who voted Democrat and what it all means.

image.caption: In the midterms, Americans vote on whether Republicans or Democrats hold the majority in CongressImage: Datajournalism Midterms 2026

blocks.text: This article was updated throughout the night. DW follows the Associated Press (AP) for when a seat is called for Republicans or Democrats.

In the 2026 midterms, Americans voted on all 435 members of the House of Representatives and 35 members of the Senate. Before election night, Republicans held the majority in both Congress chambers, if only by a hair.

Midterm elections are held every four years. The results will influence US politics for the next few years. Despite the significant executive power delegated to the presidency according to the US Constitution, the majority of federal political decisions have to be approved by Congress before they can be implemented.
Live election results: Democrats win majority in both House and Senate
For ongoing updates, go to our US midterms live blog.

In the US Senate, Democrats have managed to flip several Republican seats, winning races in Republican strongholds such as North Carolina, South Carolina, Kansas, Texas, and Iowa. With that, they have crossed the majority-line of 51 seats required to gain control of the chamber.

In the House of Representatives, all 435 seats are up for election. Democrats have crossed the threshold of 218 seats required to win the majority. That means they have flipped both chambers of Congress.
How did Americans vote: a look at demographics and attitudes

The data on voter demographics and attitudes is based on a representative survey of almost 80,000 verified voters conducted by survey and market research firm SSRS on behalf of AP and other news organizations. It builds on interviews of both early and mail-in voters as well as exit polls of in-person voters on Election Day. Where percentages of Republican and Democratic voters don't add up to 100%, the remaining percent were voters who voted for third-party candidates.
Republicans lead among white men, Democrats among younger voters

Republicans continue to make up the majority of white male voters. 55% of white men polled voted Republican. On the opposite end of the spectrum are Black women, 92% of whom voted Democrat. Remarkably, the majority of both Latino men and women voted Democrat in this election. Two years ago, Latinos were a big part of the vote that carried Trump to his second term in the White House.
Latino voters turn away from Republicans

The data shows that Republicans have lost support among all demographic groups compared to the last midterms in November 2022. Even among white men, the share of those who voted Republican fell from 60% to 55%. Among white women, the Republicans' share fell from 56% to 47%, and among Latinos, the percentage of Republican voters decreased as well.
Democrats lead among young, urban voters and college graduates
Age-wise, Democrats are strongest among young voters. Three-quarters of 18- to 24-year-olds voted Democrat. On the flipside, Republicans lead with 51% among voters aged 65 and up.

The urban-rural divide that has been part of US politics for years continues to hold. Among urban voters, 71% voted Democrat, among suburban voters, that number stands at 58%. On the other hand almost 60% of rural and small town voters were Republicans.
Democrats make up 62% of voters with a college degree. Among voters without a college degree, the split is less significant: 47% voted Democrat and 51% Republican.
It's the economy, stupid

One of the most important factors in this year's midterms is the economy. Prices for gas have increased significantly since the start of the Iran war, and everyday goods have become more and more expensive across the country as well. Almost half of all Americans say their family's financial situation is worse than two years ago.

That sentiment is not the same across the board though. Among those saying their family is better off than two years ago, 75% voted Republican and 24% Democrat. Among those saying they are worse off, only 24% voted Republican and 74% Democrat. President Trump has been saying that the country is on the upswing.
Immigration, economy, the state of democracy: What's the biggest issue for voters?

On the question of which issue facing the country is most crucial, voters are divided among party lines. Of those who said immigration is the most important issue, 89% voted Republican and only 10% voted Democrat. Anti-immigrant rhetoric has been a mainstay of Trump's speeches. He promised to ramp up deportations at the start of his second term. Many states have seen a sharp increase in activity from federal immigration agencies. ICE (Immigration and Customs Enforcement) agents have been arresting immigrants off the street, even people who have ongoing asylum application processes, for example. Trump and his supporters say these actions are necessary to make the US safer.

Among those who say that the state of democracy is the most pressing issue in the US, 78% voted Democrat. Congressional Democrats and their supporters have been saying they are concerned about how Trump ignores direct judicial orders, for example to halt deportations, or Congressional resolutions. Among those saying the economy is the most important issue, there's an almost even split of Republican and Democratic voters.
US Iran- and Israel policies

American voters are split on major foreign policy decisions made by the Trump administration. Among those saying that the joint US-Israeli war against Iran was the right decision, 91% were Republican and only 7% Democratic voters. Among those saying it was the wrong decision to attack Iran, 82% were Democratic voters and 16% were Republican voters.

The US support for Israel has been a highly controversial topic ever since Israel began its strikes on Gaza in retaliation to the Hamas terror attack on Israel on October 7, 2023. The two countries have long been partners, with the US being the most important ally for Israel, and Jewish voters a crucial demographic in the US. But as the humanitarian situation in Gaza deteriorates, support for Israel among the US population, particularly among younger people and liberals, has been wavering. Of those saying US support for Israel is too strong, 78% were Democrat voters and 20% were Republican voters. Among those saying support is about right, only one quarter was Democrat voters.
Domestic policy: dissatisfaction with Congress and country's direction

Among those dissatisfied with the House's and Senate's work, one third are Republican voters. With the extreme level of polarization in the US, reaching compromises to pass laws or approve a budget in Congress has become harder in recent years. That could be contributing to dissatisfaction.

Of people seeing their country as going in the right direction in general, only 4% were Democrat voters. Of those saying they're dissatisfied or even angry about the US's current direction, 70% were Democrat voters — and 27% Republican.

92% of those who said they approved of ICE's actions were Republican, while of those who disapproved, 86% were Democrat. Regarding Trump's tariff policy, there's a split along party lines as well, with Republican voters largely feeling they helped the economy. The president had introduced sharply increased tariffs on goods from a large number of US trading partners. Trump said the move was intended to even out unfair trade balances and protect American manufacturing. He has also used tariffs to punish countries he saw as acting against his political interests. The trade measures have made many goods more expensive for Americans.
Low approval ratings for Trump

Trump is not on the ballot, but the midterms are considered a referendum on how he and his Republicans governed the country for the past two years. Most recently, Trump's approval ratings have fallen to the lowest he has ever had, with just under 30% of Americans saying they think he is doing a good job.
In recent history, only George W. Bush has fared worse, with 25% at the end of his second term. During the 2006 midterm election, Bush's Republican Party lost control of both chambers of Congress.

articles.title: Want to end political dynasties? Here’s how you can help make it happen
articles.summary: Your signature could help push for a law that limits political families' hold on public office. Watch the video to learn how.

blocks.text: Your signature could help push for a law that limits political families' hold on public office. Watch the video to learn how.
MANILA, Philippines – Do you want to help put an end to political dynasties in the Philippines?

The People’s Initiative Coalition Against Dynasty (PICAD) is giving registered voters a way to take part through Dapat Isa Lang, a digital platform launched to gather signatures in support of a proposed nationwide ban on political dynasties.
PICAD aims to collect 7.5 million signatures by January 31, 2027, before submitting the petition to the Commission on Elections for verification.

The initiative comes amid longstanding concerns over how politics in the Philippines has become a family affair, with powerful clans dominating local and national governance. Decades of research have linked the concentration of political power among dynasties to persistent poverty, weakened checks and balances, and conditions that allow corruption to thrive.

Nearly 39 years after the 1987 Constitution explicitly mandated a ban on political dynasties, Congress has repeatedly failed to pass an enabling law, leaving the same powerful families to inherit and swap public offices unchecked.

With Congress failing to act, PICAD is turning to a People’s Initiative despite anti-dynasty bills already pending in the legislature. According to PICAD, the anti-dynasty bills pending in Congress would not effectively prohibit political dynasties.
For instance, House Bill No. 8389 only covers relatives up to the second degree within the same government unit. PICAD wants a broader ban that would cover relatives up to the fourth degree.

“The measures now before Congress do not go far enough to end the concentration and perpetuation of political power within families. If a political family can continue to hold or seek elective office simply by moving from one position or jurisdiction to another, then we have not addressed the problem the Constitution requires the law to address,” Dapat Isa Lang spokesperson and lawyer Carlo Africa said.

Under the proposed People’s Initiative law, only one family member would be allowed to hold a national elective post and another a local elective post simultaneously. The proposal also strictly forbids relatives from swapping seats or switching jurisdictions to perpetuate family control.
Registered voters can read the proposed law and sign the petition through D1L.org. The platform also provides a step-by-step guide to the process.
Watch this video to learn more about the initiative and how you can participate. – Rappler.com
